checks.finding: Met object 436535, accession 1993.132, Vincent van Gogh, 1889, oil on canvas 73.2 x 93.4 cm. Met API currently returns primaryImage DP-42549-001 in original and web-large versions, exactly matching the catalog. Two later studio variants were painted in September 1889.

Met says the Saint-Rémy countryside composition was painted on the spot; a letter to Theo dated 2 July 1889 describes the cypresses, wheat, poppies, Scottish plaid-like blue sky and impasto, and the Met distinguishes this summer painted-on-site work from 2 September indoor renditions. National Gallery of London identifies its September version as painted indoors from the earlier study. The letter is a first-person description in 1889, not proof of a claimed feeling of awe.
